page: Amazon Web Services r8i.32xlarge is an x86_64 memory-optimized instance operating on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. The platform is powered by an Intel Xeon 6975P-C processor running at 3.9 GHz, delivering 64 physical cores and 128 dedicated vCPUs through symmetric multithreading. Compute resources are supported by 480 MB of L3 cache alongside hardware support for Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) and AVX-512 instruction sets. System memory features 1024 GB of DDR5 RAM operating at 7 GHz, providing a consistent 8 GB per vCPU ratio. Local storage is not included on this instance type, and it contains no discrete GPUs, while baseline network throughput is rated at 50 Gbps.

Benchmark results show top-tier multi-threaded execution and high memory bandwidth. In stress-ng evaluations, the multi-core score reached 138375.45, paired with a Geekbench multi-core score of 22335.0 and strong Clang software compilation throughput. Small-block cached memory bandwidth registered at 10218.84 GB/sec, while uncached large-block read operations achieved 383.47 GB/sec. The instance demonstrated notable throughput in data-intensive tests, recording 218.29 million Redis SET operations per second and 33039.83 in PassMark database operations. Conversely, single-thread processing exhibits average-to-strong relative performance, such as a single-core stress-ng score of 2120.0.

The r8i.32xlarge offers high compute and memory density within a single virtual machine, minimizing multi-node communication overhead for high-capacity applications. Because the instance lacks bundled local ephemeral storage, persistent and scratch volumes rely entirely on network storage, which must be planned relative to the 50 Gbps network capacity. The resource footprint fits large in-memory databases, caching arrays such as Redis, distributed analytics platforms, and concurrent data transformation pipelines.
